title: CVMAX: Accelerator Architecture with Polar Form Multiplication for Complex-Valued Neural Networks
problem: Complex-Valued Neural Networks (CVNNs) suffer from higher computational and memory overheads than real-valued networks but are essential for applications using complex numbers; deploying CVNNs on resource-constrained devices requires energy and area optimization.
motivation: CVNNs have demonstrated superior performance in domains using complex-number operations but are underutilized due to high computational overhead; efficient hardware acceleration could enable broader deployment.
method: CVMAX is a software-hardware co-design using specialized quantization based on polar form representation (magnitude and phase) combined with shift quantization. Polar form reduces bit width and computational complexity significantly versus rectangular form. A dedicated hardware accelerator supports CVMAX data types and arithmetic operations optimized for polar multiplication simplicity.
key_novelty: Polar-form quantization and specialized hardware for low-overhead complex-number multiplication in CVNN accelerators.
contributions: Polar-form quantization reducing bit width and computational complexity
Shift quantization leveraging polar multiplication simplicity
Dedicated hardware accelerator for CVMAX operations
75% energy reduction and 4.44x speedup vs. conventional accelerators
primary_theme: Polar-form quantization for efficient CVNN acceleration
